clue.text: Espionage writer's tea in the afternoon with a northern thief

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
PM, post meridiem, marks afternoon times
a pincher is one who pinches, that is, steals

explanation.surface: A spy novelist takes afternoon tea in the company of a northern crook.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'). Chapman Pincher was a British journalist famous for books exposing Cold War spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapman Pincher made his name writing about espionage and moles within British intelligence.

clue.text: Most rude word for bottoms in bed?

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, here the rude word placed within the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
arses is the vulgar British word for bottoms

explanation.surface: A cheeky question: what's the crudest term for backsides between the sheets?
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means vulgar or rude, so the superlative is the most rude.

clue.text: One caught in spring trap?

parts.note: not a sprung snare but a person taken in by a prank played on the first day of a spring month

explanation.definitionFit: The victim of a hoax on 1 April is caught by a seasonal trick played in spring.

clue.text: Cash in my old points

indicators.note: the next pieces sit within the possessive word, signalled by in

parts.note: N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: Someone redeems loyalty points from an old scheme for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is a straightforward synonym for money in general.

clue.text: Web expert able to make money after tax

parts.note: a net is a web or mesh
a pro is an expert, a professional
fit means able or suited, as in fit to work

explanation.surface: An internet whizz earns enough to keep plenty once the taxman has had his share.
explanation.definitionFit: Accountants call earnings left once tax and costs are deducted the bottom-line gain.

clue.text: See 1
Tin can in US state

parts.note: can is slang for prison, as is pen (penitentiary)
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A tin can turns up in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin' is British slang for money, so it defines a coin, not metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is old British slang for cash, and a penny is a coin of small value.

clue.text: In Chile, to recreate Stone Age

indicators.note: to recreate is to make anew, so these letters are formed afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A plan to rebuild a prehistoric settlement in Chile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like part of the verb but belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Neolithic describes the later part of the Stone Age, when farming began.

clue.text: Section of golf club stocking brand new driver

parts.note: hose means stockings or tights
L is the learner plate on a novice driver's car

explanation.surface: A golf shop stocks a shiny new driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' reads as a verb about a shop but is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosel is the socket on a golf club head into which the shaft fits.

clue.text: Horny old Greek's vessel sounds groovy, man!

indicators.note: sounds says the letters are taken from how the words are said, not spelt

parts.note: right on is hippy slang of approval, like groovy, man

explanation.surface: A hippy enthuses about an ancient Greek drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyton was an ancient Greek drinking vessel shaped like a horn or animal head.

clue.text: When 2's caught dropping ecstasy in front of the stage

indicators.note: dropping means letting one letter fall out of the date

parts.note: victims of 2 Down are caught on the first of April, written APR ONE
E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone fooled on a spring day drops a pill in front of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 Down is APRIL FOOL, so the date when one is caught is 1 April, read as APR ONE; dropping E gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre this is the part of the stage projecting in front of the curtain.

clue.text: Lousy tune played weakly

indicators.note: a tune played may be rendered in any order of notes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor melody performed feebly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenuous means thin or flimsy, so doing something this way is doing it feebly.

clue.text: Excursion with Mary, getting flexible super savers?

parts.note: a sally is a trip or outing

indicators.note: flexible letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: An outing with an accommodating Mary in search of bargain hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link. The Sally Army is the British nickname for the Salvation Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salvation Army sets out to save souls, so its members are savers in a spiritual sense.

clue.text: Knocking back cool gin without touching the sides, chillin' at home here

indicators.note: knocking back a drink suggests the letters are tossed back in reverse
a drink going down without touching the sides passes through the inside, so the letters are taken from within the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone downs a cold gin in one at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without touching the sides' takes OOLGI from inside 'cool gin'; 'Knocking back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow house is a home where you would be chilly, playing on chillin' as relaxing.

clue.text: Crams loads on board for the return journey

indicators.note: a return journey goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to stow is to load cargo aboard a ship

explanation.surface: Cargo is packed aboard for the voyage home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crams' looks like a verb but the answer is the noun: studious types who cram.
explanation.definitionFit: Swots are pupils who study hard, cramming for exams; crams as a noun plural for such people.

clue.text: Make an example of one club dismissed for 100?

parts.note: in cricket, clubbing the ball for one run is hitting a single
a batsman who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: A cricketer who reaches a hundred and then gets out.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture: a batsman on 99 hits a single for his century and is then out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick someone out for special attention, praise or blame is to make an example of them.

clue.text: 5/4 in Forfar? Thin gruel!

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A complaint about watery porridge served in the Scottish town of Forfar.
explanation.walkthrough: 5/4 means a quarter of 5 Down, a PENNY: the old coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A farthing was an old British coin worth one quarter of a penny.

clue.text: To jog the memory, shake Belgian gripped by both hands

indicators.note: one piece held in the grip of the other

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Shaking a Belgian firmly by both hands to stir his recollection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sounds familiar and prompts recollection is said to do this, an idiom from bells summoning.

clue.text: Frayn's work upset Mrs. Hague, featuring topless poses

indicators.note: an upset arrangement is knocked over and jumbled

parts.note: Ffion Hague is the wife of the politician William Hague

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, first, letter

explanation.surface: A scandal: a politician's wife disturbed by revealing photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' is a link. 'topless' removes P from 'poses' leaving OSES, which joins FFION in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Frayn wrote this farce about a touring theatre company falling apart backstage.

clue.text: First impression of Dick Fuld era? Shockingly terrible!

indicators.note: the first impression is the opening letter of the name
shockingly suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A verdict on the reign of Dick Fuld, the Lehman Brothers boss when the bank collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful is a direct synonym for very bad or awful.

clue.text: Board not for turning; it'll be swallowed by a big fish

definitions.text: it'll be swallowed by a big fish

parts.note: a plank is a board of wood

indicators.note: turning round puts the word that follows it backwards

explanation.surface: A defiant board resists a takeover by a big player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big fish' echoes business, but whale sharks and baleen whales really do swallow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny drifting organisms are the food filtered by whale sharks and whales.

clue.text: He proclaims king that is wearing crown

indicators.note: wearing means held within, as clothing surrounds

parts.note: CR is an abbreviation for crown
R is for rex, Latin for king
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A herald announces the king in his crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier is an official who announces public news aloud.

clue.text: Radio fundraiser for Noah's shopping gallery?

indicators.note: radio means as heard over the air, by sound

parts.note: an Ark Aid charity appeal, like Live Aid, would raise money for the ark

explanation.surface: A broadcast appeal raising money for Noah's flood preparations.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered passage lined with shops.

clue.text: Ruler, having pledged allegiance, changed sides at the start

indicators.note: the first letter swaps left for right, L becoming R

parts.note: one who has pledged allegiance is faithful

explanation.surface: A monarch who had sworn loyalty switched allegiance early on.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal is a member of the ruling family, a monarch or sovereign.

clue.text: It makes sail going about the cay, having left Spain

indicators.note: going about is turning the boat, so the letters change direction and order
having left means one letter departs

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A boat tacks around a small island after leaving Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A cay is a small low island. Without E, THE CAY gives THCAY to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat is a vessel that sets sail.

clue.text: Daughter put aside US soft drink; time for Dynasty!

indicators.note: the daughter is set aside, taken out of the drink

parts.note: soda pop is American for a fizzy drink
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A girl skips her fizzy drink because her favourite TV show is on.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynasty was a glossy 1980s US television serial about a rich family.

clue.text: Second husband undressed harem in allotment

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer layer, the end letters

explanation.surface: A second husband is introduced to a harem with nothing on.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a portion allotted to someone, their part.

clue.text: Rowing brothers regularly seen in Roman ships

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: Siblings pulling oars are often spotted on Roman galleys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowing' means quarrelling: Liam and Noel Gallagher fronted this band and fought constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Britpop band was led by the feuding Gallagher brothers.

clue.text: Change oar going round the harbour

indicators.note: going round turns these letters about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Swapping oars while circling the port.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a sheltered place where ships can moor.

clue.text: Richard III featuring in science fiction parody?

indicators.note: featuring in means placed inside

parts.note: Richard the Third is rhyming slang for turd, so poo

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's king turns up in a sci-fi send-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: Richard the Third means turd.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a humorous imitation or send-up.

clue.text: Dub hospital department "doctor-lite"

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: An ENT ward branded as a lightweight version of a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub is to give a title or name to, as a knight is dubbed.

clue.text: Full of passion, Liverpool's wingers keep United quiet

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within
wingers play on the wings, the outer edges

parts.note: STFU is crude internet shorthand demanding silence

explanation.surface: Liverpool's wide men silence Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of Liverpool are L and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of lust, the strongest sexual passion.
